description: Task 5 synthesis: RLVR (exact final-answer verification) versus RLAIF (direct AI pairwise preferences) with the policy family and group-based RL procedure held approximately fixed. Numerical scales of the two rewards are not comparable; the comparison uses correctness, ranking, disagreement patterns and out-of-domain transfer.

verifier_judge_agreement_in_domain.definition: Over response pairs for the same problem where the exact verifier assigns different rewards, the fraction of pairs the AI pairwise judge prefers the verifier-correct response.

clean_correct.diagnostic_question: reference response every controlled pair is measured against
clean_correct.note: Reference arm: preference rates are undefined because it is compared against nothing. verifier_correct_rate is the share of these responses whose designated final answer matches gold.

feedback_source_summary.coverage: The verifier sees only the designated final answer, so it cannot distinguish two wrong solutions or a correct answer reached by corrupted reasoning; the judge can separate them but only through its own notion of quality.
feedback_source_summary.noise: The judge is a fixed 3B model; its labels are reproducible but not ground truth (see the Task 4 manual audit).
feedback_source_summary.exploitability: The verifier is exploitable through answer-format gaming; the judge is exploitable through style and verbosity.
feedback_source_summary.compute: One verifier call per response versus K(K-1)/2 judge calls per prompt, with the 4-bit judge loaded at runtime.
